name.text: Graphing an inclusive linear inequality in standard form

questiontext.text:
Solve and graph the following linear inequality in two unknowns:

\( \displaystyle {@A*x + B*y@} \le {@C@} \)

a) Find the axes intercepts for the boundary equation \( {@A*x + B*y@} = {@C@} \).

(Enter the numerical values for the intercepts below.)

\(y\)-intercept (when \(x = 0\)): \( y = \) [[input:ans1]]

\(x\)-intercept (when \(y = 0\)): \( x = \) [[input:ans2]]

\(y\)-intercept check: [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
\(x\)-intercept check: [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

b) Graph the inequality on the Cartesian plane below:

  • Drag the two blue points to set the boundary line. (Notice the line is solid because the inequality is inclusive: \(\le\)).
  • Drag the green Region Marker into the area that satisfies the inequality \( {@A*x + B*y@} \le {@C@} \).

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Part a: The Algebraic Boundary

To plot the boundary line \( {@A*x + B*y@} = {@C@} \), we find the axes intercepts.

First, we find the \(y\)-intercept by substituting \( x = 0 \):

\( \displaystyle \begin{aligned} {@A@}(0) + {@B@}y &= {@C@} \\ {@B@}y &= {@C@} \\ y &= {@ta1@} \end{aligned} \)

Next, we find the \(x\)-intercept by substituting \( y = 0 \):

\( \displaystyle \begin{aligned} {@A@}x + {@B@}(0) &= {@C@} \\ {@A@}x &= {@C@} \\ x &= {@ta2@} \end{aligned} \)

The boundary line passes directly through \((0, {@ta1@})\) and \(({@ta2@}, 0)\).

Part b: Graphical Representation

We plot the two intercepts on the Cartesian plane and draw a solid line through them because the inequality is inclusive (\(\le\)).

Next, we determine which region to shade using a test point. The origin \((0,0)\) is the simplest test point. We substitute \(x = 0\) and \(y = 0\) into our inequality:

\( \displaystyle \begin{aligned} {@A*x + B*y@} &\le {@C@} \\ {@A@}(0) + {@B@}(0) &\le {@C@} \\ 0 &\le {@C@} \end{aligned} \)

This statement {@origin_statement@}. Therefore, we place our region marker on the corresponding side of the solid line to indicate the shaded area.

If B > 0, shading y <= ... means shading below (right of the directed line). Inverse: true handles this. */ var ineq = brd.create('inequality', [line], {fillColor: '#4caf50', fillOpacity: 0.2, inverse: (b_val > 0)}); /* Show the marker in the origin if valid, else in a far quadrant */ var mx = (0 <= c_val) ? 0 : -8 * Math.sign(a_val); var my = (0 <= c_val) ? 0 : -8 * Math.sign(b_val); brd.create('point', [mx, my], {name: 'Solution Region', size: 6, strokeColor: '#2e7d32', fillColor: '#4caf50', fixed: true}); [[/jsxgraph]]
